Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
245 PM PDT Sat Oct 31 2026

.SYNOPSIS...An upper-level ridge offshore keeps western Washington
dry through Sunday with areas of morning fog. A frontal system
arrives Monday night, followed by an atmospheric river Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TONIGHT THROUGH MONDAY/...Light offshore flow tonight
with patchy dense fog in the lowlands by morning. Highs Sunday in the
upper 50s. Clouds increase Monday as the ridge shifts east.

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...Ensembles agree on a moist
southwest flow Wednesday into Thursday. Snow levels near 6000 feet.
QPF remains uncertain; the heaviest totals favor the Olympics.

&&

.AVIATION...VFR except IFR in fog 12z-17z.

&&

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
300 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026

.SYNOPSIS...The ridge breaks down today. A cold front crosses tonight
with breezy south winds. An atmospheric river aims at the area
Wednesday into Thursday with river flooding possible.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...Rain spreads inland this
evening. Gusts to 40 mph along the coast. Puget Sound convergence zone
showers Tuesday north of Seattle.

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...Flood watch likely for rivers
draining the Olympics and Cascades Wednesday.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Several rivers could reach flood stage Thursday.

&&
